messages:
incident-bot: PAGING on-call @oncall-alice — Severity: P1 — Syndrome: elevated tail latency for customer \"Syndicate\" on /v1/generate-stream (streaming stalls reported). Auto-alert at p99 breach > 30s.

oncall-alice: i'm oncall, ack. posting SLOs and high-level impact? can someone capture p95/p99 and regions?

ryan: quick snapshot from grafana: p95 ~ 1.2s (baseline ~0.65s), p99 jumped to 34s (baseline ~9s). error rate for streaming chunk timeouts up from 0.1% -> 4.6%. spike started ~1765556600, persisted across us-west-2 and eu-west-1.

mira: customer is single-tenant pool on dedicated nodes (pool id: synd-03). concurrent active sessions ramped from ~400 -> 1.8k in last 5m. noticed many long-prefix requests (avg prompt tokens ~3.2k).

oncall-alice: thanks. can we confirm model variants serving and if any failover happened?

ryan: serving stack: redlm-v1 (base FP32), redlm-v1-quant (int8 fallback available). routing shows 100% to redlm-v1 on synd-03. no automatic fallback triggered — because nodes saturated and streaming stalls cause live request stalls not explicit node failures.

mira: logs show repeated KV cache eviction thrash on worker-12 and worker-15: \"kvcache_evictions=1249\" and GC cycles spiking. that aligns with many unique long prefixes.

eng-sre-lead: likely hypothesis: combined long-prefix workload + sudden concurrency spike => KV cache thrash -> increased decode latency -> streaming chunk timeouts. Prior mitigations: reduce batch windows, enable prefix caching warmup, or route to lower-memory model.

product-sam: customer impact? are they seeing partial responses or full disconnects? need to inform account team.

eva-ml: from chat logs we saw streaming stalls where client-side reconnects are frequent. that looks like in-flight decoder stalls at the token streaming layer. quality not degraded but latency severe.

oncall-alice: immediate plan of action (T-minus):
1) reduce incoming concurrency to synd-03 by applying soft throttle at the edge (10s window, -30% concurrency)
2) enable canary routing: route 20% traffic from synd-03 -> redlm-v1-quant in eu-west-1 (lower mem footprint, slightly lower quality)
3) increase autoscale target for synd-03 by +2 GPUs and reduce batching window to 15ms
4) collect KV cache metrics + heap profiles from worker-12/15

ryan: running throttles now: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/internal/throttle -d '{"pool":"synd-03","reduction":0.30}'` -> 202 accepted.

opsbot: Action executed: soft-throttle applied to pool synd-03 (-30%). Canary route created: 20% -> redlm-v1-quant (eu-west-1). Autoscale request queued: +2 gpus.

mira: canary look: initial 20% shows p99 ~ 6.7s (better). streaming stalls reduced for canary traffic. KV eviction rate on worker-12 down 78% after throttle.

eng-sre-lead: good. keep throttle + canary for 20m, monitor p99, and if stable then consider 50% routing or gradual roll to quant. document timeline for postmortem.

product-sam: p99 improvement percentage for customer? need numbers for account update.

ryan: before mitigations p99=34s, after canary p99 for canary subset ~6.7s, overall pool p99 down to ~18s after throttle+canary. chunk timeout error rate down from 4.6% -> 1.1%.

oncall-alice: okay cc: @eng-sre-lead @mira @ryan — keep me posted every 5m. if we don't get below p99<10s in 20m, escalate to platform oncall and prepare evacuation plan (route entire pool to dedicated quant or fall back to hosted multi-tenant).

eng-sre-lead: assigned POC: ryan (lead) and mira (customer ops). I'll prepare incident doc skeleton.

mira: starting heap profile and kv cache dump now: `kubectl exec -it worker-12 -- curl localhost:9090/debug/heap` -> uploading to incident artifacts.

opsbot: Autoscale event: requested +2 GPUs in us-west-2, provisioning in progress (est ETA 4m).

eva-ml: note for postmortem: evaluate prompt length caps and pre-warm KV cache strategies (prefix sampling + async warming). also check tokenization differences leading to unexpected prefix cardinality.

product-sam: draft message to customer (short): \"We're investigating elevated streaming latency starting at 14:10 UTC affecting a subset of your requests. We've applied mitigations that have reduced tail latency; our engineers are monitoring. We'll follow up with a timeline and root cause within 24 hours.\" ok to send?

oncall-alice: ok to send, please add: \"no data exfiltration, only performance impact\".

ryan: quick sanity: stack traces show repeated stalls in attention_kernel.cu around KV lookup hot paths. capturing line-level traces.

mira: after 8m mitigation: p99 steady at 8.9s for pool, error rate 0.4%. can start gradual increase of canary to 40% to see response.

oncall-alice: increase canary to 40% now. opsbot?

opsbot: Canary update executed: 40% -> redlm-v1-quant.

mira: 2m after increase: p99 across pool ~7.4s, KV evictions remain low. customer chat indicates fewer reconnections.

eng-sre-lead: hold pattern — maintain reduced batch window and autoscale until next steady-state 10m. collect traces for postmortem.

product-sam: account notified. they replied: \"thanks — please keep us posted, we saw timeouts in live demos earlier.\"

noncall-alice: logging timeline and tags for postmortem: incident-start=1765556600, mitigations=[throttle-30%,canary-quant-40%,autoscale+2GPUs], owners=[ryan,mira,eng-sre-lead].

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity remains P1, current pool p99=7.4s, customer impact reduced but not fully resolved. next update in 5m or on status change.

eng-sre-lead: if stable for 20m we'll step down severity and transition to follow-up doc. otherwise escalate to infra leads for kernel-level hotfix.

mira: capturing final metrics snapshot now and saving artefacts to /incidents/1765556666/artifacts.tar.gz

oncall-alice: thanks team — keep an eye, i'll stay on til we step down.

ryan: noted, continuing trace collection and KV analysis. will attach repro prompt patterns to ticket.

opsbot: autoscale completed: +2 GPUs provisioned in us-west-2 (nodes: g4dn-33, g4dn-34).

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled if not resolved in 2h.

mira: leaving for handoff — @oncall-alice you're primary.

oncall-alice: ack. closing real-time updates for now; documenting postmortem tasks.

eng-sre-lead: good work. postmortem checklist: timelines, kernel traces, KV-cache metrics, prompt corpus sample (top 50), mitigation timeline, customer impact summary, action items (kv warmers, prompt caps, autoscale tuning).

incident-bot: Thread closed for active updates. Further discussion should happen in follow-up ticket #INC-1765556666."
